subject: science
instructions: Use the supplied investigation, model, or data. Record observations and distinguish evidence from inference.
Follow every safety direction. If required material, adult approval, or a safe alternative is missing, stop.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain problem definition in your own words and give or identify a valid example.
Use a diagram, model, quotation, data display, map, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of criteria constraints and stakeholders.
Apply data-driven comparison in a new realistic situation. Show the process or cite evidence.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, unsafe choice, or design flaw involving iterative modeling; correct it and explain why.
Connect problem definition with scientific argument and communication. Explain how the ideas support, constrain, contrast with, or build on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit project: Complete an engineering or research capstone tied to forces, waves, life science, Earth science, or environmental systems.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy or quality, and one next question.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated accuracy or fidelity criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated evidence and reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated application or performance criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated checking and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Engineering and Scientific Argument Capstone?
